## Purpose

Compare current delivery and readiness evidence with the intended project outcome: a restricted, self-hosted Option B LeadLab application available before 2026-09-11. Assess material variance, confidence, forecast, attention items, and decisions across the project without treating local implementation as staging or launch acceptance. This run will prepare recommendations and proposed control updates only; it will not approve a release, accept a deliverable, change scope, approve a change, assign ownership, establish a baseline, close a control item, or reconcile canonical records.

## Performance Boundary

The assessment covers the current approved Option B delivery increment and its launch path across:

- Scope and acceptance evidence, including recent approved feature increments and remaining browser, responsive, staging, and launch checks.
- Schedule and forecast, including the conditional 2026-09-04 go/no-go, conditional 2026-09-07 launch target, fixed 2026-09-11 program start, and overdue Gate 1 reassessment.
- Quality and security, including automated verification, authenticated browser evidence, protected access, participant-data handling, and activity logging.
- Environment and operations, including target runtime, database, deployment, rollback, private storage, HTTPS, backup and restore, monitoring, incidents, email, queue, scheduler, and operational ownership.
- Governance and stakeholders, including unresolved project decisions, technical and IT ownership, and LeadLab Director final acceptance.

This run does not perform a standalone schedule-control run, validate scope acceptance, assess unrelated financial performance, approve the proposed deployment-research choices, or authorize staging or production use.

## Tailoring Decision

| Factor | Project evidence | Tailoring effect |
|---|---|---|
| Criticality | The application protects restricted participant content and is intended to be available before 2026-09-11. | Use a formal review with explicit evidence, confidence, gates, decisions, and PM review. |
| Scale | The team and product are small, but the MVP spans access, Classroom, Q&A, calendar, administration, security, and operations. | Assess the material cross-domain signals rather than producing a broad low-value metric inventory. |
| Duration | The fixed program date is imminent; the conditional go/no-go is 2026-09-04 and the conditional launch target is 2026-09-07. | Time-box the review around the next decision gate and identify recovery or fallback actions without inventing durations. |
| Complexity | Target environment, staging, mail, queue, scheduler, participant data, ownership, and final approval remain linked uncertainties. | Use an integrated variance and dependency view, with gaps separated from verified results. |
| Approach | Delivery is iterative: local implementation precedes staging and launch acceptance. | Compare actual evidence with the intended outcome and conditional forecast; do not equate local tests with release readiness. |
| Maturity | A control root, registers, scope records, schedule-management plan, and delivery evidence exist, but RAG tolerances, evidence refresh cadence, and several owners are unconfigured. | Use existing carriers, record confidence and limits, and surface missing thresholds and ownership rather than creating unsupported measures. |
| Governance | The requester and IT team control project direction; the LeadLab Director provides final launch acceptance. | Prepare recommendations and proposed updates; reserve approvals, assignments, baseline decisions, and acceptance for the PM or authorized approver. |

## Assessment Method

Use the smallest evidence-based set of performance views:

| View | Current comparison basis | Treatment of missing evidence |
|---|---|---|
| Outcome readiness | Approved Option B outcome and 2026-09-11 need date | Report readiness as conditional or blocked where staging, operations, or acceptance evidence is absent. |
| Scope and acceptance | Approved requirements, backlog, recent approved changes, local tests, and browser or staging evidence | Separate implemented locally, conditionally accepted, and not evidenced. |
| Schedule | Conditional go/no-go and launch targets, Gate 1 trigger, open actions, dependencies, and current progress | Do not create a baseline or calculate unsupported float, duration, or recovery capacity. |
| Quality and security | Automated tests, static checks, local access tests, browser evidence, participant-data controls, and activity-log evidence | Record source-inspection or local-only results as limited confidence when runtime evidence is missing. |
| Environment and operations | Gate 1 pack, deployment research, email operations note, and dependency or decision records | Treat unknown target conditions as gaps and candidate research as unapproved evidence. |
| Governance and ownership | Current decisions, actions, issues, dependencies, risks, and final acceptance condition | Keep unassigned owners and proposed decisions visible; do not assign or close them. |

Project-level RAG tolerance thresholds are unconfigured. The assessment will therefore use explicit condition labels, evidence confidence, and consequences rather than inventing numeric thresholds.

## Minimum Output

1. An integrated performance assessment as of 2026-09-02.
2. A variance table covering intended outcome, scope and acceptance, schedule, quality and security, environment and operations, and governance.
3. A conditional forecast with confidence, assumptions, dependency effects, and fallback implications.
4. A prioritized attention and decision list linked to current records.
5. Proposed process metadata or dashboard-view updates only, with PM-only actions clearly separated.
6. A next review trigger before the 2026-09-04 go/no-go decision.
